extracted.intended_audience: Potential offerors/applicants (industry, academia, nonprofits) preparing white papers or full proposals in response to ONR BAA N00014-22-S-B002 (STAMP).
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit white papers or full proposals in response to the Office of Naval Research STAMP Broad Agency Announcement (N00014-22-S-B002), complying with eligibility, formatting, registration, content, evaluation, and award administration requirements specific to this BAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall scientific and technical merit / responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall scientific and technical merits of the proposal and responsiveness to the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the degree of innovation and soundness of the technical concept; awareness of the state of the art and understanding of the scope of the problem (including associated technical risk), significance and originality of the technical approach, and effort needed to address/solve the problem; and anticipated impact within the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and capabilities of Principal Investigator and key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall facilities and capabilities of Principal Investigator and key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes offeror’s facilities — extent to which the proposal reflects a coherent, coordinated collection of distributed facilities for research, development, prototyping, pilot manufacturing, and workforce development — and qualifications, capabilities, and experience of the proposed PI, team leader, and key personnel critical to achieving objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structure suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses suitability of the organization for performing the proposed work; academic and industrial partnership structure with well-defined royalty/licensing/revenue methods; mechanisms and policies to ensure robust participation by small and medium-sized businesses and large enterprises; and well-structured and coherent Intellectual Property management across contractual R&D arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential relevance to DoD / contribution to component mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential relevance to the Department of Defense (DoD) and contribution to a DoD component mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators judge how the proposed work contributes to DoD needs and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of funds and proposed cost share (full proposals only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of funds, to include proposed cost share in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not applicable to white papers. Cost share is optional but may improve chances; if proposed, the Government requires the recipient’s cost share to be specified. Government will consider state/local funding and private sector investment; cost sharing includes cash and third-party in-kind contributions such as equipment, facilities, and manpower. Refer to DoDGARS § 32.23 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation weighting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative importance of evaluation criteria for white papers and full proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White papers: Criteria 1 (technical merit), 2 (facilities/personnel), 3 (organizational structure), and 4 (DoD relevance) are equally important. Full proposals: Criteria 1–5 are equally important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal evaluation approach / selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: How proposals are reviewed and selected for recommendation and award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are not evaluated against each other (no common work statement); reviewed as received. Scientific/technical community makes recommendations; Contracts and Grants Awards Management conducts cost analysis, responsibility determination, and funds availability checks. Selection recommendation does not guarantee award. ONR may remove offerors who fail to reach agreement on terms/price or who do not timely provide requested information.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting rules for white papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper size 8.5 x 11 inches; margins 1 inch; single-spaced; font Times New Roman 12 point; page limit 5 pages excluding cover page. If emailed, file must be Word 2016 or PDF compatible and email size limit is 5 MB per email.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required content elements for white papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include a mandatory Cover Page (specific ONR cover sheet link) with Program Officer information (found in Section G). Technical concept (description of technology innovation, industry and risk areas); Organizational structure (entities and relationships, PI and key personnel); Facilities (description of cohesive distributed facilities); Future DoD relevance and contributions; Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate. Offerors should consult Technical POC regarding desirability of white paper submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory cover page inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: White paper will not be accepted without the required cover page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover Page templates/links provided for contract and grant submissions; FedConnect will not accept a white paper unless the Cover Sheet is included. Program Officer information is a required field on the cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-proprietary Statement of Work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must include a non-proprietary version of the Statement of Work (SOW).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not put proprietary data or markings in or on the non-proprietary SOW. For classified proposals, an unclassified SOW must accompany the classified submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary data marking and legend
rubrics_metrics.description: How to mark proposal data that offeror does not want disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title page legend text provided: data shall not be disclosed outside Government except to evaluate the proposal; specifies how to identify which sheets are restricted and requires each restricted sheet to be marked with a legend: 'Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of this proposal.' Offerors should mark each page that contains proprietary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security classification and classified submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Security expectations and procedures for classified proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are expected to be unclassified; classified proposals are permitted. If classified proposal is submitted and selected for award, the resultant contract will be unclassified but must be accompanied by an unclassified SOW. Classified proposals must be mailed to ONR Document Control Unit with specified outer/inner envelope addressing and marking instructions (outer envelope unmarked, inner envelope stamped with classification and addressed to the cognizant Technical POC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration in SAM and Unique Entity Identifier requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All offerors must be registered in SAM and provide a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must maintain an active SAM registration with current information while they have an active Federal award or application under consideration. A Federal agency may not make an award until applicant has complied. SAM accessed at https://www.sam.gov/SAM/.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect registration and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: FedConnect is the portal ONR uses for white paper submission and requires registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: obtain DUNS (historical language present), register with SAM to receive UEI, obtain SAM MPIN if first to register for the organization, create FedConnect account. FedConnect how-to guide link provided; FedConnect support contact info provided. Do not use FedConnect Message Center for technical questions; email POCs in Section G instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility limited to national technology and industrial base
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility restricted to persons and organizations that are part of the national technology and industrial base as defined in 10 U.S.C. § 2500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All responsible sources within this base from academia, industry, and research community may submit. HBCUs and MIs encouraged but no set-asides. Both small and large businesses may submit. FFRDCs and DoE national labs are not eligible to receive awards (team arrangements allowed only if permitted). Navy labs, military universities, warfare centers, and other DoD/civilian agency labs cannot directly submit white papers or full proposals; UARCs may submit unless precluded by their contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teams and information sharing expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Team submissions are encouraged but offerors must be willing to cooperate and exchange software, data, and other information in an integrated program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should be willing to collaborate and integrate with other contractors and participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument type selection and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible award instruments include procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, TIAs, OTAs for research, and OTAs for prototype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each instrument has legal definitions and expectations: grants (no fee/profit, limited substantial involvement), cooperative agreements (substantial involvement expected), TIAs (may provide 50/50 cost share to the maximum extent practicable; no fee/profit), OTAs (50/50 cost share to the maximum extent practicable and work must not duplicate existing DoD programs). Model contracts/grants links provided as examples; current FAR/DFARS/NMCARS/ONR clauses govern in conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted fundamental research definition and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR follows the USD (AT&L) memorandum definition of 'contracted fundamental research' for DoD contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes research funded by RDT&E Budget Activity 1 (Basic Research) or Budget Activity 2 (Applied Research) performed on campus at a university. Research funded by BA2 not on-campus, BA3, or BA4 does not meet the definition. ONR will place no restrictions on unclassified contracted fundamental research except as required by statute/regulation/EO. Prime contractors must identify subcontracted work that constitutes fundamental research and include statements confirming scope and determination. Non-fundamental research may require restrictions and DoD pre-publication review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting plan requirement for contracts > $750,000
rubrics_metrics.description: Large businesses and non-profits proposing contract awards exceeding $750,000 must provide a Subcontracting Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan must contain all elements required by FAR 19.704 and FAR 52.219-9, as supplemented by DFARS 252.219-7003. If the offeror has a Master/Individual/Subcontracting Plan, a copy shall be submitted. Plans are reviewed for adequacy; failure to negotiate an acceptable Plan can make offeror ineligible for award. Small businesses are exempt from this requirement. Offerors should propose realistic goals ensuring small business participation consistent with DoD subcontracting goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business participation and outreach expectations (contract awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is committed to providing meaningful prime and subcontracting opportunities for various small business categories and socio-economic concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large businesses and non-profits must submit a subcontracting plan; ONR will facilitate prime/subcontractor connections by posting small business contact information (not an endorsement). Small businesses interested in subcontracting should email specified information (company name, POC, brief tech description, keywords) to the ONR Small Business Director; do not include proprietary information as it will be publicly posted. PTAC assistance resources are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing optionality and impact on selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors may propose no cost share and remain eligible; proposing cost share may improve chances of receiving an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cost share is proposed, it must be specified; government will consider state/local funds (non-Federal) and private sector investment. Cost sharing includes cash and third-party in-kind contributions (equipment, facilities, manpower).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model contracts and grants precedence clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Model contracts and grants are provided as examples and do not override governing clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of conflict between example documents and current FAR, DFARS, NMCARS, or ONR clauses, the current clauses govern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced cybersecurity compliance prior to award
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain offerors may be required to demonstrate ability to comply with enhanced cybersecurity requirements prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Appendix 2, Section F, Federal Award Administration Information, Part 2, Administrative and National Policy Requirements, paragraph (9) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecommunications and video surveillance prohibition and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on procuring or contracting for covered telecommunications equipment or services as defined in Section 889 of the NDAA; offerors must represent and disclose use/intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must review SAM excluded parties list. They must represent whether they will provide covered telecommunications equipment/services and whether they use covered equipment/services; if affirmative, they must provide detailed disclosures (entity producing equipment, unique identifiers, CAGE, OEM/distributor status, brand/model numbers, description of use, PSC for services, explanations relevant to permissibility). The clause explains the statutory prohibitions and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility demonstration — ability to integrate government, industry, and academia
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible organizations should demonstrate ability to bring government, industry, and academia together for joint development and commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence may include academic and industrial membership structures with royalty/licensing/revenue methods; effective mechanisms and policies for robust participation by small/medium businesses and large enterprises; well-structured and coherent IP management; and a coherent, coordinated collection of distributed facilities for collaborative R&D, prototyping, pilot manufacturing, and workforce development.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII purpose and manufacturing readiness focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of Manufacturing Innovation Institutes (MIIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MIIs are public-private partnerships to accelerate commercialization by developing/scaling technologies in MRL 4-7, providing shared access to equipment and capabilities, and supporting education and workforce development. MIIs are part of DoD MII network and should create national impact in their focus areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII design tenets
rubrics_metrics.description: Design tenets for DoD Manufacturing Innovation Institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: industry-driven public-private partnerships led by independent non-profits leveraging existing resources; federal funding matched by industry/academic/state cost share; domestic industrial commons via shared IP and facilities; investments in applied and industrially relevant manufacturing technologies; access for small/medium manufacturers; education and workforce development investments; harmonization with DoD/service modernization priorities and commercial applications; MII size/scale sufficient for long-term economic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — hire and retain key management staff
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must hire and retain key management staff focused on operation and management of the institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Director/CEO expected full-time; key management staff (deputy directors, C-suite) expected >75% time commitment to the MII.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — establish and manage physical and virtual infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must establish and manage appropriate physical and virtual infrastructure scaled to mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While leveraging member-owned infrastructure, the MII should operate infrastructure appropriate to its mission and ensure long-term operating costs are covered by long-term revenues from operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — conduct annual planning
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must employ annual planning processes with broad stakeholder involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual Program Plan must include detailed budget with revenue strategy, plans to manage business-plan changes aligned with technology roadmap, and mechanisms for partnerships with federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — develop business plans to maintain viability
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must develop and implement business plans to become financially viable and world-leading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should generate revenue, bring public/private entities together, drive commercialization, and use successes to attract ongoing investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — define structure and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: MII should operate under a non-profit with independent governance and impartiality toward members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MII must be neutral when making sub-award determinations and selecting governance representatives; should not compete with members for providing products/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — continuously improve operations
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must incorporate lessons learned and periodically update integrated technology roadmaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create mechanisms to assess progress and widen impactful R&D while focusing on transformative value and commercialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — involve industry and academia
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must define transparent by-laws and strategies for recruitment and active participation of a broad range of members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage private/public resources, national labs, university centers, government institutions; engage supply-chain stakeholders and regional economic organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — engage with DoD and government partners
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must develop working relationships with DoD and other government partners and include them in decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodate expectations for DoD participation in strategic and technical decision bodies and identify investment opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — develop technology roadmap and execute project calls
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must create time- and event-based roadmaps for maturing technologies and demonstrate a framework for defining/selecting/executing projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may address technology, manufacturing, workforce development, or demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — foster education and workforce development
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must support domestic technical workforce development through education, internships, and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop curricula with educational institutions (K-12, universities, community colleges), provide internships/co-ops, and bridge gaps from R&D to full-scale production.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — develop manufacturing technology and prototyping
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must be at cutting edge of applied research with access to state-of-the-art equipment and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct R&D and prototyping to demonstrate desired future states for DoD and commercial customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — foster commercialization
rubrics_metrics.description: MII should target investments toward projects intended to result in commercially successful products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on demonstrations and prototypes that enable industry partners to commercialize technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — create and maintain IP-protected innovation ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must enable pre-competitive collaboration while protecting IP and promoting commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster inventor ownership of IP, protect background IP, and encourage commercialization through licensing/productization.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — coordinate development of industry standards
rubrics_metrics.description: MII should coordinate industry and Standards Development Organizations to identify and accelerate needed standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position the MII to influence standards development relevant to its technology focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — generate cost share and continued investment
rubrics_metrics.description: MII must attract cost share and continued investment from members and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage ecosystem to stimulate investment in relevant technologies via the MII and broader industrial base.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — enhance defense capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: MII should pursue manufacturing technology development that enhances defense capabilities while enabling commercial applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include DoD modernization priorities in technology roadmaps; target technologies with both defense and commercial applications when they contribute to defense capabilities.
